headline: Qatar's route from 77 to 142 million tonnes runs through a revised first-train date
deck: North Field East, South and West take Qatari capacity to 142 mtpa by 2030. The schedule on the first train has moved.
excerpt: QatarEnergy's North Field expansion is the largest single addition to global LNG supply this decade, lifting capacity from 77 to 142 million tonnes a year by 2030. Startup on the first train has been reported as moving to early 2027.
content:
No single project shapes the LNG market of the next decade more than Qatar's North Field expansion, and Gastech opens in Bangkok this week with its schedule under revision.

The programme takes QatarEnergy's liquefaction capacity from 77 million tonnes a year to 142 million tonnes by 2030, through three phases: North Field East at 32 million tonnes, North Field South at 16 million, and North Field West at a further 16 million. Package scopes on the West phase cover the critical equipment for two LNG mega trains, including six gas turbines, twelve centrifugal compressors and integrated power systems.

First gas from North Field East had been expected in the middle of this year. Reported schedules have since moved, with construction interrupted earlier in 2026 and the contractor Chiyoda subsequently confirming that staff would return to site to resume work, with startup on the first train now indicated for early 2027.

A slip of two or three quarters on a project of this size is not unusual in absolute terms and is significant in market terms, because of what depends on it. Buyers who contracted against a delivery window plan their own supply portfolios around it. Competing sellers with capacity arriving in the same period have their commercial position altered by it. And the shipping market, which orders vessels years ahead against expected trade flows, is sized on the assumption that the volumes arrive when scheduled.

The scale of the mega train configuration is worth stating plainly for a construction readership. A single LNG train at this capacity is one of the largest process units built anywhere: cryogenic heat exchangers, very large refrigeration compressor strings driven by gas turbines, extensive stainless and aluminium piping, and storage tanks holding liquid at minus 162 degrees. Modules are fabricated in Asian yards and shipped, and the site work is heavy civil, mechanical erection and commissioning at a scale few contractors can staff.

Qatar's cost advantage in this market is structural. The North Field is a very large, low-cost resource with associated liquids, and the incremental cost of adding capacity at an existing complex is well below that of a greenfield project elsewhere. That is what allows the country to expand into a market whose price direction over the next decade is uncertain.

The commercial question the Bangkok programme is set up to address is where the volumes go. A substantial share of Qatari LNG has historically moved to Asia under long-term contracts, and the next tranche arrives as buyers in the largest growth markets are pressing for shorter terms and more flexible destination clauses.

Gastech runs at BITEC Bangkok from 14 to 17 September.
author: Jakson Gudawela
scheduledReason: Written before Gastech opens in Bangkok on 14 September. It works from the published programme and independently verified project data, and makes no claim about anything said or announced at the event.
